assessments.closureRisk: Low—owner next actions are concrete and unblocked; closure is a single experiment cycle.
assessments.dominantCost: Designing genuinely distinct encounter variants that perturb the right axes without breaking boundedness.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Fund the construction of 2–3 materially different bounded encounter variants and re-run causal-episode probes across them.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002 priors are partly fixed-encounter overfit; perturbation will separate surviving generalization from brittle priors.

assessments.dominantCost: Physical/portable gate execution time; low research content.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable/physical gates and commit if they pass.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Mechanism selection is complete; remaining work is mechanical acceptance and release.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Mostly mechanical closeout; low expected frontier delta relative to G-AF3.

assessments.whyNotFirst: Exploratory with a conditional build; lower expected value than G-AF3's direct generalization test.

assessments.topologyHypothesis: Control-path repair is admitted but live experiments are externally blocked on DNS recovery.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high—blocked on external host provisioning.
assessments.dominantCost: External infrastructure acquisition; not addressable by research budget.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent host, verify immutable deployment kit, provision separated signers.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control; dominant blocker is absence of an independent Linux/systemd host.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Explicitly a negative control with a dominant external admission blocker; deferred.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the only candidate that is both unblocked and at a genuine decision frontier: AF002 is complete, the current fixed Genesis has almost no environment variation, and the next unit directly tests which AF002 priors survive perturbations—a high-value ambiguity-reduction/prior-narrowing step that is closable with the owner's own next actions. R-P5 is close to closure but is mostly mechanical (final gates, commit, self-release); low marginal research value per unit. HOST-PKG is exploratory but the packaging question is only justified "if measurable" and may be a no-op. H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery despite an admitted control-path repair, so it cannot close now. F-C2-BLOCKED is explicitly a negative control with a dominant external blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host), so it is deferred.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether G-AF3's perturbation variants reveal that some AF002 priors are fixed-encounter overfit (prior-narrowing) versus survive across materially different encounters (prior-generalization).
result.selectionFalsifier: If G-AF3's encounter variants are not actually materially different (i.e., the owner cannot construct 2–3 bounded variants that perturb topology/position/resource/target), the experiment degenerates to a no-op and the budget would have been better spent on R-P5's final closure or HOST-PKG's packaging audit.
